answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a shared market, then slash that bond when a challenge proves its identity or actions violate the rules. One operator can still create many sybils, but must lock real capital for each one and risks losing it; the cost grows with the influence sought. A lagoon market might set bonds by exposure, while a zephyr of cheap accounts cannot cheaply shift the horizon of prices.
